reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in the multi-track pooling module, which extends traditional single-track memory models by incorporating appearance information from all concurrently tracked objects. This is mathematically modeled using bilinear LSTM memory vectors, where each track's memory is augmented with a concatenation of other tracks' memories. The resulting pooled memory vector $\mathcal{M}_{\text{pool}} = \text{Concat}(\mathcal{M}_t^{\text{pos}}, \mathcal{M}_{\neg t}^{\text{neg}})$ serves as a richer template for discriminative matching. The bilinear LSTM memory function $\mathcal{L}_{\text{mem}}(x_t) = \sum_{i=1}^{n} \langle h_i^{t-1}, x_t \rangle$ computes similarity scores across multiple templates, enabling robust appearance matching even under visual ambiguity. Greedy data association then selects the best match based on summed memory scores, avoiding complex multi-frame optimization while maintaining real-time performance. The failure mode arises when similar-looking objects share overlapping appearance features, causing misclassification despite pooling. This is mitigated by leveraging inter-track contrastive learning, where negative examples from other tracks refine the positive track's representation.
